small_guidance:
- The GEMM is M=128, N=16384, K=16384 — M is tiny so BLOCK_M=32 or 64 is right, but add larger BLOCK_N (256) and BLOCK_K (64-128) configs with num_stages=4 and num_warps=8 to better hide the long K-loop latency; consider configs like {BLOCK_M:64, BLOCK_N:256, BLOCK_K:128, num_warps=8, num_stages=4} and {BLOCK_M:32, BLOCK_N:256, BLOCK_K:128, num_warps=8, num_stages=4}.
- Add a GROUP_M block-swizzle (group along N since M is small — i.e. swizzle pid_n in row-groups of 4-8) for better L2 reuse of x across N tiles, since x (128×16384=8MB) fits cache but weight (1GB) does not.
- Fuse the bias add and the softmax max-reduction's per-tile partial max into the GEMM epilogue (write per-row tile max alongside output), so the softmax pass only needs to reduce M×(N/BLOCK_N) partials instead of streaming N=16384 values three times.
large_guidance:
- The dominant cost is the 128×16384×16384 GEMM (~70 GFLOPs) plus three full passes over the 128×16384 output in softmax. Redesign as a single fused "linear + softmax" persistent kernel: one program per output row, keep the entire 16384-wide row in registers/SMEM by tiling N, compute partial GEMM tiles, and run an online softmax (Welford-style running max + renormalized sum) so the activation matrix is never materialized to HBM.
- Alternatively, since M=128 is very small, treat this as a "skinny GEMM": one program per row (or row-pair), iterate N tiles in the outer loop and K tiles in the inner loop, accumulate softmax statistics online, then do a second pass over N tiles re-computing the dot-products (or caching them in HBM) to write normalized outputs — this trades recompute for one fewer HBM round-trip of the activation.
- Store weight in a layout that matches the access pattern of the fused kernel (e.g. [N_tile, K] tiles contiguous) precomputed once in __init__, so each N-tile's K-loop is a fully coalesced stream of contiguous memory.
